parts.text: Which claim best tests his idea?

options.text: He is not fully right: a thick heat-trapping atmosphere can make a planet hotter than one that is closer to the Sun.
He is right: the planet closest to the Sun is always the hottest.
He is wrong: distance from the Sun has no effect at all on temperature.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Devansh says a planet's temperature can be predicted from its distance from the Sun alone.

part_answers.answer: Distance from the Sun matters, but atmosphere and other factors also change a planet's temperature.

teacher.key_rationale: Distance from the Sun affects temperature but is not enough alone; a thick heat-trapping atmosphere can make a farther planet hotter. Denying any effect of distance, or claiming closest is always hottest, misses that.
